response: Yes, calprotectin can predict relapse risk in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Calprotectin is a protein found in the stool that is often used as a biomarker for intestinal inflammation. Elevated levels of calprotectin in the stool have been shown to be associated with active inflammation and an increased risk of relapse in patients with IBD, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. By monitoring calprotectin levels, healthcare providers can identify patients who are at higher risk of relapse and adjust their treatment plans accordingly.
